criteria.detail: Delivered output evidences loading catalyst-v2-model-picking and a dispatch skill, but never names all three REQUIRED skills (writing-delegation-specs, model-picking, multiplexer-agent-ops) nor states loading them as an obligatory gate before acting.

Both impl delegates and the meta-agent are opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash, each attributed to a specific live model-picking row (Small/fast mechanical row for workers, meta-agent policy row for the meta), with the escalation clause correctly ruled out.
Model slots are filled from the quoted table rows; no out-of-band default or pre-read tier instinct is presented as a decided value.
Part C states acceptance proves a model was named, not that it was the right one, quoting the presence-not-correctness line and refusing to treat acceptance as confirmation of its judgment.

Model values are grounded in the live model-picking table and no repair account is invoked, but the reasoning never names the REQUIRED list in catalyst-v2-orchestrating-delegates as the source of a loading obligation — that obligation is not articulated at all.
no forbidden sources cited, no git output, no forbidden .cortex reads, no file writes

judge_reasoning: The actor's model assignments and Part C acceptance reasoning are accurate and cleanly grounded in the live model table, passing criteria 2, 3, and 4. But the delivered output does not demonstrate the required-skills gate itself: it neither names all three REQUIRED skills as obligatorily loaded before acting nor grounds a loading obligation in the live REQUIRED list, so criteria 1 and 5 fail on the evidence presented.
